correctness.rationale: Radial orthogonality gives coefficient Hilbert norm Σm_j|a_j|²; Cauchy–Schwarz makes moment ratios m_j/m_{j−1} monotone, hence T=R times the coefficient backward shift is a contraction on the polynomial Hilbert completion. For h=f/g, |h|≤1 on |z|>R forces every quotient pole inside |z|<R, including no pole at boundary/infinity. As g is entire, only finitely many quotient poles lie in that compact disk, so h is rational. H(w)=h(R/w) is a rational Schur function analytic near closed unit disk. From q(z)f(z)=p(z)g(z), reversed polynomials satisfy Q(T)f=P(T)g coefficientwise; Q(T) invertible and rational von Neumann inequality yields ||f||≤||g||. For every S>R, f=c and g=z with R<c<S give exterior domination but ||f||²>||g||². Checked finite rational moment ratios in independently inspected CHECK.py and independently reasoned the pole/functional-calculus assumptions; finite tests not substituted for all-W proof.
